topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening administrative framing, learning outcomes, and thematic overview for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Cellular and Genetic Basis of Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an accumulation of genetic alterations that causes a failure of normal developmental differentiation and tissue architecture.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how local tissue invasion and distant metastasis distinguish malignant tumors from benign ones both clinically and histologically.

topics.label: Stepwise Progression and Classification of Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate the stepwise progression of precursor lesions into invasive cancer and outline the system used to classify and name these tumor types.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physiological mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause systemic disease and patient death.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence Across Tissues and Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distribution of cancer incidence and mortality across different human tissue types and diverse animal species.

topics.label: Principles and Practice of Clinical Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the rationale, diagnostic methods, and clinical challenges of population screening programs for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing for the lecture, reminding students of the learning outcomes and looking ahead to practicals and upcoming sessions.
